fact: Nile Post describes the NBI as Uganda's government-owned national fibre-optic network connecting public institutions and offering access to a nationwide network; no places or lengths given. Dated by the article (2026-10-09).

NITA-U contracted CITCC on 2022-04-22 (NITA-U/Supplies/21-22/001) to supply, install and commission NBI/EGI Phase V, extending the backbone to about 62 districts; Hansard of 2023-12-06 says implementation was expected to start early 2024.

fact: ICT Minister Baryomunsi told Parliament on 2023-12-06 that existing NBI coverage was about 50 per cent of the country, with roughly 62 districts not covered by phases I-IV.
Phase V builds on NBI Phases I-III (2006-2013) and Phase IV (2018), which were built; Phase V extends fibre to sub-county level (per BU Chinese Loans to Africa database).
Contractor CITCC signed commercial contract NITA-U/SUPLS/21-22/0001 on 2022-04-22 for Phase V: 3,604 km of backbone with 51 backbone sites, plus last mile to 800 government sites.

fact: NITA-U says President Museveni launched Phase V in Karamoja, delivering an additional 5,845 km of fibre across 63 districts; date not given, after loan effectiveness on 2024-09-18.
system: National Data Transmission Backbone Infrastructure Phase V

fact: Phase V extends the fibre backbone to districts and sub-counties not reached by Phases I-III (2006-2013) and Phase IV (2018); the Finance Ministry's 2023-11-27 proposal said Phase V would take backbone coverage to 83%.

NITA-U states that Phase 5 of the National Backbone Infrastructure, launched nationally in Moroto District on 4 December 2024, was extended to Kanungu District in December 2025, as one of 63 districts in a programme laying over 5,000 km of new optical fibre and 21 solar-powered transmission sites.

The Ministry of ICT's FY2025/26 policy statement reports 1,567 sites connected to the National Backbone Infrastructure and 4,387 km of optical fibre cable laid in total, as the position at the time of writing (March 2025, the document's published date); it names no regions.

Bayobab Uganda (MTN Group subsidiary) launched on 6 May 2025 a 260 km fibre route along the Uganda Railway line from Kampala to Malaba on the Kenyan border, built December 2024 to February 2025, which Bayobab says completes the Kampala-Mombasa backbone and carries over 1 Tbit/s.
NITA-U reports that under the National Backbone Infrastructure, fibre optic connectivity was extended to 41 additional districts, with work continuing towards nationwide coverage.

The ICT minister told Parliament's committee that the National Backbone Infrastructure is largely used by government agencies with few private-sector clients, and its commercialisation is to move to UTel.
Xinhua reports the first four NBI phases have covered nearly 50 percent of Uganda, laying 4,172 km of fibre across 63 districts.
Xinhua reports President Museveni launched construction of NBI phase five on 4 December 2024, financed by China EXIM and implemented by Huawei.
NITA-U says the first four NBI phases laid 4,387 km of optical fibre connecting 53 district headquarters, 11 major border stations and 1,480 ministries, departments and agencies.

The ministry says government has laid 4,387 km of optic fibre across 57 of 135 districts (42%), with 1,567 government sites (MDAs and local governments) connected to the National Backbone Infrastructure (Zawedde, via Business Focus).

The Daily Monitor says NBI phase one (completed June 2008) laid 168 km linking Kampala to Mukono, Bombo and Jinja, and phase two (2009 to 2013) laid 1,400 km linking Busia, Mbale, Soroti, Lira, Gulu, Fort Portal, Kasese, Mbarara and other towns.
